finding: The guard of BR-135 lives outside the ledger, so the ledger itself allows the edge from blocked to dispatched for any reason. Ledger.transition accepts blocked to dispatched for every caller. resume_gates_refusal guards it in cmd_resume_gates, and MARK_DISPATCHED_SOURCES guards it again in cmd_mark_dispatched (dispatch:1846-1857). Today these are the only two callers that ask for dispatched, so no path skips the guard. The next subcommand that calls ledger.transition(id, StoryState.DISPATCHED) must remember a third check. Ledger.return_story already shows the other pattern: the guarded edge is a method of the ledger, and the method refuses by itself. Fix: in dispatch_lib.py, add Ledger.resume_gates(story_id), which raises TransitionError with the text of resume_gates_refusal and then sets dispatched. Make Ledger.transition refuse blocked to dispatched, so only that method takes the edge. cmd_resume_gates calls the method, and cmd_mark_dispatched drops its own check.
why_this_severity: The code exists only on the story branch, so it is not in use. Both callers that ask for dispatched check the guard, and CG-09-IT-01 shows that mark-dispatched refuses a blocked entry (no to fails_purpose). The rule of BR-135 is written twice, and every later caller of Ledger.transition must repeat it, because the generic edge set does not carry it.
